subject: brutalistBlock
pitch:
Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A raw board-marked concrete housing slab in the Unité d'Habitation tradition: seven storeys of deep loggias on chunky pilotis, a separate stair and lift tower, and a sculpted roof terrace with chimneys, a gym vault and a paddling pool.
spec.layout: Static architecture, 48 m wide (x), 34 m tall (y) and 20 m long (z, from -11 at the back to +9 at the front). The long main facade faces +Z. From the ground up: a thin plaza slab (y 0 to 0.25); a forest of massive tapered concrete pilotis (y 0 to 5) with a glazed lobby between them in the middle; the slab block itself (x -24..24, z -7..7, y 5..27, seven storeys of 22/7 m each, floor lines at y = 5 + 22/7 * k for k = 0..7); on the front a 2 m deep egg-crate of loggias (z 7..9) made of full-height fins and projecting floor slabs, each cell holding a recessed window and a coloured infill panel; a free-standing stair and lift tower against the back (x 14..22, z -11..-7, y 0 to 34) that rises 7 m above the roof; and a sculpted roof terrace (y 27 to 31) with chunky ventilation chimneys, a curved gym vault, a pool and a parapet. The style is raw concrete everywhere: heavy chamfer-free blocky masses, board-marked formwork lines (thin darker or lighter strips as small parts), staining under every ledge, and a few saturated primary-colour panels (red, yellow, blue, green) as the only accents. The silhouette is a long horizontal slab on legs with one tall vertical tower, and the whole thing reads as heavy and monolithic. No glossy surfaces. Windows are dark glass, and about one in five glows warm yellow.

parts.builds: Everything at ground level under the slab. A thin plaza slab (x -24..24, z -7..9, y 0 to 0.25) in concreteDark with paving joints as thin boardMark strips. Two rows of massive pilotis at z = -4.5 and z = +4.5, at x = -22, -14, -7, 7, 14, 22, each tapering from 2.6 m wide at the base to 1.6 m wide at y 3, then a chunky tapered 'foot-to-capital' shape up to y 5, with a pronounced squat blocky look. They are board-marked: thin horizontal darker and lighter strips every 0.4 m on the faces, plus stain streaks (concreteStain) in a tall thin box below the caps and mud at the feet. Extra heavy twin piers at x = ±24 on the end walls. Between x = -4 and 4 sits a recessed glazed lobby (z -3 to 5, height to y 4.4) with a dark glass front, steel mullions, a lit warm interior band (glassLit), a deep cantilevered concrete entrance canopy (z 5 to 8, y 4.2 to 4.7, concreteLight with a rust edge strip), a wide stepped approach (3 steps) and a side ramp with steel handrails, plus a letter-number emblem plaque 'B1' built from small parts in panelYellow next to the door. Add three rows of ribbed soffit beams (long thin boxes in concreteMid) hanging under the slab (y 4.6 to 5), two bike racks and two bench slabs, and two bollard lamps with lampWarm tops. Everything is made from primitives: boxes, tapered frustums, cylinders.
parts.attaches: Pilotis tops end exactly at pilotisTop / slabUnderside (y 5) where slabBody starts. The plaza top is plazaTop (y 0.25). The lobby sits at lobbyCentre. The tower stands separately at z < -7 and its foot is the tower part's.

parts.builds: The main concrete mass of the slab and its flanks: a core box x -24..24, z -7..7, y 5..27 in concreteMid (the front loggia part builds on its face at z = 7). It has two blank gable end walls at x = ±24 (each 14 m deep by 22 m high) with a deep board-marked relief of long thin horizontal strips alternating boardMark and boardMarkLight, a big graphic emblem built from panelRed / panelYellow / panelBlue slabs on the left end (a large stacked-rectangles mural, 6 by 12 m, seated 0.1 m proud), narrow slit windows in a staggered column near each back corner, and rain staining (concreteStain tall thin streaks from every ledge). The rear facade (z = -7) has a horizontal strip-window band on every storey (dark glass, thin steel mullions every 2 m, a few windows in glassLit) with projecting 0.3 m concrete sills and lintels in concreteLight, and a recessed shopping-street level on storey 4 (y 14.4 to 17.5) where the facade steps back 0.8 m behind a continuous glazed band with panelWhite shopfront boards. A slightly proud horizontal floor-edge band (0.3 m high, 0.1 m proud, concreteLight) at each floor line on the rear and ends. Top edge: a heavy 0.5 m concrete cornice ledge all round at y 26.5 to 27 (concreteLight). The inner joint with the tower on the rear face between x 14 and 22 is left plain: a recessed vertical slot (shadowSlot) 0.2 m wide at x = 14 and x = 22 on z = -7.
parts.attaches: Sits on pilotisTop (y 5). Its front face (z = 7, slabFrontFace) carries the frontFacade part, so keep the front face a plain concreteMid plane. Its back face (z = -7, slabBackFace) meets the tower part at towerJointToSlab. Its top (y 27, roofDeck) carries the roof part.

parts.builds: The egg-crate loggia facade covering the entire front (z 7 to 9, y 5 to 27, x -24..24): 13 full-height vertical fins at x = -24 + 4*k for k = 0..12 (0.5 m wide, 2 m deep, concreteLight, board-marked with thin strips, with the fin edges slightly darker at the soffit); 8 projecting floor slabs (z 7 to 9, 0.35 m thick) at the floor lines y = 5 + 22/7*k for k = 0..7 in concreteMid with a lighter front-edge strip; each slab has a thin steel railing (a top rail and a few posts) along its front edge z = 8.9, merged where possible. Each of the 12 x 7 cells is recessed: a window set in the back wall (dark glass `glass`, about every fifth lit with `glassLit`, steel frame, a mullion), a lower solid balcony-wall infill panel (1 m high) and in about 40% of cells a coloured wall panel behind the loggia (panelRed, panelYellow, panelBlue, panelGreen, panelWhite in a deliberate Mondrian-like pattern, same pattern per column on each storey so vertical stripes read, with a few random exceptions) seated at z = 7.1. Add: under-slab shadow strips (shadowSlot) and drip stains (concreteStain) under each slab, a tiny coloured laundry line or potted plant in a few cells (moss/panelRed small parts), the building number '12' as chunky blocks in panelYellow on the left of the second floor slab face, and a thick vertical concrete numbering band on the middle fin. Use merged geometry per colour and bone for the repeated infills to stay in budget.
parts.attaches: Back plane at slabFrontFace (z = 7), flush with slabBody. Bottom at floorLine0 (y 5) over the pilotis part's canopy region; top ends at y 27 under the roof parapet. The fins' outer edge is frontBalconyEdge (z = 9).

parts.builds: The free-standing stair and lift tower behind the slab, x 14..22, z -11..-7, y 0 to 34 (height 34 m is the model's tallest point). A massive board-marked shaft in concreteMid with thin horizontal formwork strips (boardMark / boardMarkLight) every 0.4 m, a heavier base plinth (y 0 to 1.2, concreteDark), a deep cantilevered cornice at the roof and a smaller lift-motor room on top (x 15..21, z -10.5..-7.5, y 31 to 34) with a cantilevered concrete lid (0.6 m overhang, concreteLight) and louvre slots (shadowSlot). The back face (z = -11) has a full-height vertical glazed stair slit 1.2 m wide (dark glass with steel mullions every storey and diagonal stair-landing silhouettes behind as small parts, a few landings lit with glassLit), flanked by narrow slit windows. Seven small cantilevered landings or access gallery stubs project from the slab-facing side of the tower at each floor line y = 5 + 22/7*k, built as short concrete bridges (x 16..20, z -7 to -7.001 stubs, 1.2 m deep platforms on z -7 to -8) with steel railings, and the entrance on the ground floor with a canopy, double doors in panelBlue, a big panelRed number '12' on the left side face, and a lamp. Left and right faces carry staggered square window punches (dark glass, concreteLight reveal frames). Rain stains below each ledge. A thin steel lightning mast with a red tip on the lid top.
parts.attaches: Its front face (z = -7) touches the slabBody rear face at towerJointToSlab; the landings stub into the slab at each floor line. Its foot is on the plaza level y 0 (a small paved step apron in concreteDark). Its shaft passes the roof deck at towerRoofLevel (y 27) and tops out at towerTop (y 34); the roof part stays at x < 14 or z > -7 and never overlaps the tower's box.

parts.builds: The sculpted roof landscape on top of the slab, y 27 to 31, x -24..24, z -7..7 (not inside the tower box). A continuous parapet of 1.0 m height (y 27 to 28) in concreteLight with a thin lighter coping strip on top and board-marked strips on the faces, with drainage scuppers (shadowSlot) and rain streaks. Terrace floor in concreteDark. Features: (1) a big curved gym or nursery vault (a half-cylinder shell lathe/sweep 10 m long, 5 m wide, peaking at y 31.0) near x -14, z 0, in concreteWarm with ribbed beams (thin boxes) every 1.5 m and a glazed end wall in dark glass and a door in panelYellow; (2) three chunky sculptural ventilation chimneys at x = -3, 3, 8 (tapered boxes with deep slots and a cantilevered cap, concreteMid, height to y 31, one with a panelRed band); (3) a rectangular paddling pool (x 10 to 13.5, z -4 to -1, recessed look with a rim of concreteLight and `pool` water slab, a few steps) and a shallow bench ring around it; (4) a sun-terrace with a running track made of thin curved boardMarkLight stripes on asphalt-colored paving (a flat rounded rectangle path) around x 0..8; (5) a staircase block up to the gym vault (stepped boxes); (6) a few planters with moss, three flagpole stubs or lamp posts (steel with lampWarm tips), skylight pyramids with glassLit panes near x = -20; (7) a rooftop water tank (a cylinder with steel bands) at x = -20, z = 2, height to y 30.6. All details must be seated on the deck; keep the lowest roof piece at y >= 27 and the tallest at 31.
parts.attaches: Sits on roofDeck (y 27) over slabBody, inside its x/z footprint, with parapet outer faces flush with the slab faces. It leaves the tower region x 14..22, z < -7 alone, and the tower rises past it at the back.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a static brutalist housing block with no joints, and I'm settling on dimensions loosely inspired by the Unité d'Habitation but scaled down. I'm leaning toward roughly 12 m wide, 24 m tall, and 40 m long.

I'm breaking the block into parts: the pilotis and ground level, the main slab body with its ribbed concrete, a front facade of loggias and brise-soleil, a rear facade with access, a stair and lift core tower, and a roof with terrace, ventilation stacks and a parapet.

I'm settling the long facade on the +Z side, so the slab runs along X at about 50 by 32 by 18 metres. The core tower will sit at the rear, rising above the roof, with its exact placement still being worked out.

I'm laying out the pilotis as a flat ground box that spans the whole block, with a row of tapered legs spaced about every 8 metres along the length.

I'm placing the pilotis as a row of chunky tapered legs about every 8 metres, with two rows front and back, and I'm adding the entrance lobby, canopy and steps at the centre. Next I'm turning to the main slab body, which I'm treating as a concrete mass with windowless gable ends, slit openings and floor-line courses every 3 metres.

I'm weighing how many parts the budget allows, and a per-cell approach for all the loggias would blow past the limit, so I'm looking at continuous strips for the front facade instead.

I'm going to size the frontal loggias and fins across the facade, and I'm weighing whether a per-cell layout fits the part budget or whether I should merge the infill panels by colour instead.

I'm reworking the core tower's footprint so it stands clear of the slab, pushing it out to the rear and extending the overall depth to fit. I'm also checking that the pilotis box doesn't overlap the tower's footprint.

I'm checking the pilotis box against the slab, settling on the pilotis spanning x from -24 to 24 so the legs line up with the slab ends. The core tower's footprint stays clear of the pilotis box, and I'm keeping the overall size at 50 by 34 by 20 with the z range running from -11 to 9.

I'm settling the core tower's footprint and making the overall size 48 by 34 by 20, then working through the tower's features: a board-marked shaft with vertical slit windows, chamfered corners, a cantilevered lift-motor cap, a ground entrance with canopy, and landing balconies at each floor.

I'm now sizing the roof: a parapet, a rooftop terrace with sculpted ventilation stacks, a curved gym vault, and a ramp, and I'm giving it about 120 parts. The lift overrun sits above the roof inside the tower's own box, and I'm budgeting the pilotis, slab, front facade, tower and roof at roughly 150, 170, 280, 150 and 120 parts.

I'm checking the part budget, which comes to 870 against a limit of 900, so it fits. Next I'm setting the storey height at 22/7 metres so seven storeys exactly fill the slab from y=5 to y=27, with floor lines at each level. For the front facade I'm laying out 12 bays of 4 metres across the full width, with 13 fins, and the balconies projecting out to z=9.

I'm settling on a colour palette of grey concrete tones, with a warm concrete and formwork-line shade, plus dark shadow and glass tones, a glowing window yellow, steel, and rust, and a set of primary accents in red, yellow, blue, green, white, moss, and a wet-stain brown.

I'm settling the palette and the mount list, and noting that the pilotis and the tower will carry the floor flag while everything else stays off. The pilotis box tops out at y=5 to meet the slab, the roof begins at y=27, and the front facade joins at z=7 while the tower joins the slab's rear face at z=-7. I'm also setting a thin plaza slab over the ground and writing out each part's coordinates explicitly.
